event_confirmation: JetBlue release of 2026-10-13 (ir.jetblue.com, also stockhouse.com/news/press-releases/2026/10/13/...): Q3 2026 call Tuesday 2026-10-27 at 10:00 a.m. ET. JetBlue has issued its release before a 10:00 ET call on every prior print (baseline: 7 of 7 bmo by 8-K 2.02 acceptance), so the session is bmo. The TipRanks 'Nov 3' row is a cadence estimate and is superseded by the company release.
conviction_note: The Q3 numbers were pre-released on 2026-09-10 and the stock has since fallen 45% in 20 sessions on fuel and on a creditor group hiring PJT and Akin Gump. The print turns on the balance sheet (Sept 30 liquidity, any financing or creditor plan) and on the Q4 guide. Peers put Q4 fuel at $4.55-4.80/gal against JetBlue's $3.96 Q3 assumption, so a deeply negative Q4 guide is very likely. Against that sit more than 30% of float short, an all-time low, a $750m covenant that UBS estimates is well covered at year-end, and a +10.5% reaction to a similar setup in July. Findings net to +1.2. p_up is 52 rather than higher because the sign runs against a +9.6 vol-point put skew and bonds at 42 cents. abs_move 20 comes from the 21% option-implied move. That gives (2*0.52-1)*20 = +0.8.
bar: Q3 2026: the company's own 2026-09-10 pre-release (8-K 7.01, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158463/000115846326000089/jblu-20260910.htm): ASMs +1.5-3.5%, RASM +17-20%, CASM ex-fuel +6-8%, fuel $3.96/gal. That implies revenue of about $2.76-2.88bn against Q3 2025's $2.32bn. Street consensus has one current source (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/JBLU/estimates): EPS -$0.53 and revenue $2.876bn, at the top of the guided range. MarketBeat (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/JBLU/earnings/) shows -$0.36 from two estimates and looks stale. Because the EPS bar is disputed, every reported-quarter finding is capped small. No sourced Q4 consensus was found, so the guidance findings are capped too. print_vs_bar_pct is revenue at the guided midpoint (~$2.82bn) against $2.876bn, nudged up because JetBlue raised RASM in September on strong demand.
positioning_check: Short interest is 'above 30% of float' per GuruFocus, 2026-10-22 (https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9137509/jetblue-jblu-shares-hit-record-low-amid-rising-short-interest-ahead-of-q3-earnings); it names no source and gives no days to cover. The last FINRA settlement found is 2026-08-14: 96.2m shares short, 4.1 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/jblu/shortinterest), up from 95.5m on 2026-07-31. Bloomberg reported on 2026-10-08 that short sellers were 'piling in' (https://news.bgov.com/bankruptcy-law/jetblue-bonds-fall-deeper-into-distress-as-short-sellers-pile-in). Baseline: 25d skew +9.6 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 2.61, ATM IV 214%, event-implied move 21.15%, run-up -20.8% over 5 days and -45.4% over 20, 0% from the 52-week low. Average 20-day volume is 28.5m shares, so 96m+ short is about 3-4 days. This is a crowded short at an all-time low, with the options market paying for a crash tail.

findings.finding: Q3 is largely pre-released, but the fuel assumption is likely a little light. JetBlue's 2026-09-10 update guided Q3 fuel at $3.96/gal off the 2026-09-04 Brent curve, with CASM ex-fuel raised to +6-8% for ATC and weather. Southwest's Q3 fuel came in at $3.92 against its own prior $3.70-3.75 assumption, so late-quarter fuel ran above earlier curves. JetBlue is unhedged, so an overshoot of $0.05-0.10/gal on ~220m gallons is about $11-22m, or $0.03-0.06 a share, against a -$0.53 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline reactions: +10.5% (Q2 2026), +1.21%, -6.89%, -11.86%, +6.65%, +2.7%, -25.71%. The reported quarter was pre-released in September, so this line has mostly been seen already.
findings.why_not_priced: The $3.96 figure is the company's own and is what the bar is built on. The Southwest overshoot (published 2026-10-21) suggests the late-September curve ran higher. If that were priced, consensus would sit below the guide-implied loss; the single available consensus, -$0.53, is roughly at it. Small, and inside a quarter the company has already described.
findings.independence: Southwest Q3 2026 release: fuel $3.92/gal vs $3.70-3.75 assumed (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000092380/000009238026000104/er-9302026xerdoc.htm; https://whtc.com/2026/10/21/southwest-airlines-cuts-2026-profit-forecast-as-fuel-costs-spike/). This is a peer proxy, not JetBlue's number.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide will be built on fuel far above anything JetBlue has guided this year. United guided Q4 at $4.80/gal (2026-10-21, Q4 EPS $0.50-1.50 vs ~$1.76-1.88 consensus), Southwest at ~$4.55/gal off the 2026-10-15 curve (Q4 EPS $0.55-0.80 vs $0.82 est.), and UBS models JetBlue at $4.85. JetBlue's Q3 guide was $3.96 and its July full-year guide assumed $3.49 with -2% to -5% operating margin, so the FY guide must be cut or suspended and Q4 will show a deep operating loss. JetBlue has no hedges.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 brought a weak outlook plus better-than-expected fuel recapture (nearly 50% recaptured), and the stock went +10.5%. The Q3 2025 print brought -11.86% and Q4 2024 brought -25.71%; the baseline does not say which line drove those. Peers' sharply below-consensus Q4 guides this month drew muted reactions (UAL -0.8% premarket, LUV +1% after hours).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. JetBlue is down 45% in 20 sessions, Morgan Stanley and Goldman have cut estimates and targets for fuel, and UBS already uses $4.85. The unpriced part is the size of JetBlue's own Q4 margin, the size of its fuel recapture, and whether the 2026 guide is withdrawn. If fully priced, peers' muted reactions suggest the guide alone would not move JBLU much.
findings.independence: Southwest Q4 at $4.55/gal (https://whtc.com/2026/10/21/southwest-airlines-cuts-2026-profit-forecast-as-fuel-costs-spike/); UBS $4.85 Q4 assumption (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/jetblue-airways-aktie-ubs-stuft-auf-neutral-hoch-senkt-kursziel-auf-350-us-dollar).

findings.finding: The balance sheet is the line this print turns on, and the facts point both ways. (a) A senior creditor group holding the $2bn TrueBlue-backed 2031 notes and the ~$742m secured loan has hired PJT Partners and Akin Gump (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026-10-24/25). The notes fell to 42 cents from ~80 earlier in October and the stock fell ~16% on 2026-10-26. (b) Against that, June 30 liquidity was $2.17bn of cash and investments plus an undrawn $600m revolver, against a $750m quarter-end minimum-liquidity covenant on the TrueBlue debt. UBS estimates ~$660m of H2 burn at $4.85 Q4 fuel and ~$1.6bn year-end liquidity, plus a possible $250m draw on a facility agreed in Q2. Scheduled debt repayments are only $236m for the rest of 2026 and $478m in 2027, and the company claims >$6bn of unencumbered assets. The 10:00 ET call is management's first chance to answer the creditor news. A Sept 30 liquidity figure well above the covenant reassures; an announced liability-management plan or adviser hire dilutes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July 2026 the 2031 notes fell to 84 cents and JetBlue scheduled a fixed-income investor meeting on liquidity (Bloomberg, 2026-07-23). The Q2 print that followed reacted +10.5%. That is one precedent where a liquidity scare before the print was followed by relief.
findings.why_not_priced: The creditor news is priced, with a 16% drop on 2026-10-26 and bonds at 42. What is not priced is the company's own Sept 30 liquidity number and its answer. Bonds at 42 imply a high restructuring probability inside about a year, while UBS's arithmetic puts year-end liquidity at about twice the covenant. If the market believed UBS, the notes would not trade at 42. Financing is a question here: no new company financing has been announced, so there is nothing yet to sign on use of proceeds. The sign stays near zero with a very wide band.
findings.independence: The creditor hire is also reported at https://onemileatatime.com/news/jetblue-creditors-hire-advisers-stock-bonds-sink-bankruptcy-looms/ (2026-10-24) and https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/26/jetblue-airways-tumbles-16-as-creditors-hire-restructuring-advisers-united-airlines-rises-3-delta-edges-higher/ (2026-10-26). The liquidity and maturity schedule is at https://viewfromthewing.com/jetblue-stock-fell-below-3-how-close-is-bankruptcy-and-will-united-buy-it/ (2026-10-21) and the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158463/000115846326000076/ex991-earningsreleaseq22026.htm). The UBS liquidity view is secondhand, via goldesel/FMP. One fact (the balance sheet) supports both readings, which is why they are filed as one finding.

findings.finding: The print lands on a crowded short at the bottom of a capitulation. Short interest is reported above 30% of float (GuruFocus, 2026-10-22), from 96.2m shares at 4.1 days to cover on 2026-08-14. The stock is -45.4% over 20 sessions and -20.8% over 5, at its all-time low ($2.16 intraday on 2026-10-26). Put/call OI is 2.61. Any reassurance on liquidity or the creditor talks hits a short base of roughly 3-4 days of volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +10.5% on the Q2 2026 print after a pre-print bond selloff and a run-in drawdown. No sourced history of squeezes on this name beyond that.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the market's own state, so it is not a fact the market has missed. The point is that it makes the reaction to anything short of a restructuring announcement asymmetric upward. The +9.6 put skew is paying for a Chapter 11 or dilution tail that the CEO has ruled out for 2026 and that the maturity schedule does not force before 2029. If the squeeze risk were priced, call IV would be bid relative to puts. It is not: skew is +9.6.
findings.independence: FINRA settlement via https://equibles.com/stocks/jblu/shortinterest (96.2m, 4.1 days, 2026-08-14); Bloomberg 2026-10-08 'short sellers pile in' (https://news.bgov.com/bankruptcy-law/jetblue-bonds-fall-deeper-into-distress-as-short-sellers-pile-in).

findings.finding: Demand and revenue are strong and were raised in September. Q3 RASM guidance went to +17-20% (midpoint 4 points above the prior guide), with 'no meaningful signs of demand elasticity' and 'early Q4 booking trends are encouraging'. Peers who reported since confirm record or double-digit revenue: UAL record $17.9bn, LUV record revenue and an EPS beat, ALK revenue +14%. That supports a Q4 RASM guide high enough to recapture part of the fuel increase, and Q2 recaptured nearly 50%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: the release led with fuel recapture 'exceeding expectations', and the stock went +10.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 RASM raise is public. The unpriced part is the Q4 RASM guide and the recapture rate, which no source carries. A stock down 45% into the print says the market is weighting fuel and the balance sheet, not unit revenue. If revenue strength were weighted, the drawdown would track bonds less closely.
findings.independence: Southwest record Q3 revenue and EPS beat (https://whtc.com/2026/10/21/southwest-airlines-cuts-2026-profit-forecast-as-fuel-costs-spike/); Alaska Q3 revenue +14% (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Alaska+Air+Reports+%24147+Million+Third Quarter+Loss+as+Revenue+Reaches+%244.3+Billion). These are peer proxies.

findings.finding: The JetForward long-range targets are at risk of withdrawal: $850-950m incremental EBIT by 2027, ~$1.2bn by 2028 and 2028 EPS of at least $1.00. Morgan Stanley warned in mid-October that prolonged fuel inflation threatens 2027 cost targets, and FCF is described as turning positive only around end-2027 into 2028 'if things go right'. A withdrawal or a push-out on the call would be a guidance negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not sourced for this line specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: At $2.30 the market already treats a $1.00 2028 EPS (2.3x) as not credible, so a withdrawal is mostly priced. What is left is the signal a withdrawal would send to creditors.
findings.independence: Morgan Stanley fuel note, secondhand via https://stockstotrade.com/news/jetblue-airways-corporation-jblu-news-2026_10_14/. Inference, not a company statement.

findings.finding: Carl Icahn cut his stake below 5% (13D/A Amendment 6, event date 2026-08-18; 12.53m shares, 3.32%) after selling about 8.1m shares at $4.73-5.28. That removes the activist floor, and the remaining 12.5m shares are a possible seller.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: filed two months ago, and the stock has halved since. Filed for completeness.

findings.finding: United's CEO, asked on United's 2026-10-21 call about JetBlue's loyalty bonds at 'half of par', said 'I have nothing new to add'. United's CFO said its enlarged liquidity was 'absolutely 100% not' for an acquisition. JetBlue and United are tied through the Blue Sky loyalty and interline partnership, which the call may update.
findings.why_not_priced: A strategic floor would show up as a stock that holds while the bonds fall. It did not: the stock fell with the bonds. So the market assigns little takeout value, and only a Blue Sky economics update on the call could add anything.

findings.finding: Small insider selling into the drawdown: a Form 144 on 2026-09-30 and a Form 4 on 2026-10-02, with four sales and no buys over three months (83,253 shares per GuruFocus).
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial size. It is public on EDGAR.

outside_window.finding: CreditSights (2026-10-15) projects a JetBlue liquidity crunch by late 2027. The largest maturity is ~$1.84bn in 2029. These are solvency horizons beyond the window and resolve only through later filings.

lessons_applied: Rule 3 and the 'two readings of one document' rule: merged the draft's +2.0 'liquidity headroom vs covenant' and -1.5 'creditor group hired PJT/Akin' into one financing finding at +0.3 with a -12 to +10 band. Both rest on one balance sheet and pointed in opposite directions.

Rule 4 and 'what has worked' (covenant arithmetic is not a document): the liquidity-headroom half rests on UBS's model and covenant arithmetic, not a company number, so it was shrunk inside the merge. No financing has been announced, so there is no use of proceeds to sign.
Rule 6 (bar has one source; Chartmill and MarketBeat disagree; no Q4 consensus): reported-quarter fuel finding -0.5 to -0.3; Q4 fuel-guide finding capped.
Rule 1 (reaction-function veto): peers' well-below-consensus Q4 guides drew muted stock reactions this month, so the Q4 fuel-guide finding went from -2.0 to -1.0.
Rule 7 (sign against a strong skew): positioning finding +2.5 to +2.0, with the reason the skew may be wrong written into why_not_priced; p_up 53 to 52, which takes expected_move from 1.2 to 0.8.
Rule 5 (proxy and inference smaller, not dropped): demand +1.0 to +0.8, long-range-target withdrawal -0.7 to -0.5, Icahn -0.3 to -0.2, United +0.3 to +0.2.
Unchanged: abs_move_pct 20 (the 21% implied move; a guidance change pushes it up and the pre-released Q3 pulls it down, which roughly cancel), print_vs_bar -1.0, and the insider-selling finding.
